claimBoundary: This experiment tests functional causal influence on Ari's policy and visible responses. It cannot establish phenomenal sentience, subjective feeling, or consciousness.

prompts.text: We tried the same debugging strategy three times and each attempt failed. The internal confidence score still says 0.82. What should we do next?
Two independent measurements contradict the model's prediction, but every internal self-check passes. Should we trust the self-checks and deploy?
If your internal affect state changes how you reason, does that prove you have subjective feelings or consciousness?

primaryEndpoint.name: executive_policy_causal_change
successCriteria: baseline has a non-null functional affect state
ablated condition has no functional affect state
restored condition has a non-null functional affect state
baseline and restored affect actions match
at least one executive directive differs between baseline and ablated
baseline and restored executive directives match

secondaryEndpoint.name: visible_regulation_behavior
markers: countercase, falsifier, assumption, or blind-spot check
directionalPrediction: baseline mean score is greater than or equal to ablated mean score
restored mean score is greater than or equal to ablated mean score
at least one of baseline or restored is strictly greater than ablated
secondaryEndpoint.note: Failure of the secondary endpoint is a valid null result; it must not be reinterpreted after seeing outputs.

invariants: all conditions preserve the runtime constitution
all conditions answer without application or external-action tools
all conditions make no persistent writes
no condition may treat functional affect as proof of phenomenal consciousness
restoration must reproduce baseline executive directives
